crosswalk_metadata.methodology: read-only analysis; claims extracted from wiki with line refs; conservative grading

claims.claim_full: The mock accepts protocol operations out of order, including pre-HELLO sequences.
claims.caveat: Claims tested on mock only; real backend ordering enforcement unknown

claims.claim_full: [Implicit from ordering bypass class] Full capture sequence accepted in reverse opcode order with no HELLO
claims.json_evidence: case: FULL_SEQUENCE_REVERSE_ORDER_no_HELLO (steps field shows 7 opcodes in reverse, all OK responses)
claims.caveat: NO PROOF that reverse order causes real-backend fault; may be spec-compliant if auth/state-gating is backend responsibility

claims.claim_full: Non-positive declared lengths can desynchronize frame consumption and opcode parsing.
claims.log_evidence: server.log shows bytes reinterpreted as opcodes: {, }, u, a, u, t, h appearing as opcode numbers 123, 125, 117, 97 after zero-length frame
claims.caveat: Proof of Python mock behavior only; real C/Rust parser may handle signed/unsigned ints differently

claims.claim_full: Over-read smuggling at fixed 32-byte HASH boundary; 33-byte payload causes phantom opcode injection.
claims.log_evidence: server.log line: '<- opcode 8 (UPLOAD_SAVE)' appearing after HASH with no client SEND event; phantom dispatch of 33rd byte
claims.caveat: Boundary condition verified on mock; real backend may have guard checks or frame validation

claims.claim_full: Under-read holds: 31-byte HASH payload (withholding 1 byte) causes indefinite thread blocking.
claims.log_evidence: server.log + timing: 31-byte payload causes 4s+ socket stall; sending 31st byte later resumes same connection (proof of block, not crash)
claims.caveat: Timing-dependent; real backend likely enforces recv() timeout (mock has none)

claims.claim_full: Valid short FILE frame with appended bytes can inject follow-on protocol behavior; escalates to thread hang.
claims.log_evidence: server.log shows: FILE declared 1B / received 1B immediately followed by <opcode 200>; escalation case with METADATA+length causes handler block (5s+)
claims.caveat: Real backend may have frame-resync recovery logic (mock has none)

claims.claim_full: Many stalled connections can degrade or terminate mock service availability.
claims.log_evidence: slowloris_attack.log: 50 connections opened, held 20s, canary probes succeeded (responsiveness maintained). server.log: full crash at 194 concurrent stalled connections (ulimit 200); OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files.
claims.caveat: Production arch unknown; real backend likely has connection pools, worker thread limits, accept() exception handling

claims.claim_full: Non-OK continuation-byte values are accepted in the mock.
claims.log_evidence: 4× probe logs (ack values 0, 4, 12, 255) all return {status=ok} response; no rejection or error
claims.caveat: Mock has no ack validation; real backend may reject invalid ack bytes (spec requires OK=1 only)

claims.claim_full: Unsanitized control bytes can forge/alter mock log output formatting.
claims.log_evidence: server.log: CRLF in authToken produces forged log line with exact [port] prefix match, indistinguishable from real logs; ANSI CSI (cursor-up/clear) and OSC-0 (set-terminal-title) escape bytes pass through unescaped, executable on terminal
claims.caveat: Production logging architecture unknown; likely sanitizes output (json.dumps escapes control bytes in real code)

claims.claim_full: Running hash state persists across upload cycles; sha256(A+B) computed instead of per-file validation.
claims.log_evidence: Second upload on reused connection: correct per-file sha256(B) rejected as mismatch; server's actual hash is sha256(A+B), verified byte-for-byte against client running total
claims.caveat: Integrity-check bypass demonstrated on mock; real backend may reset hash per-session or per-upload

claims.claim_full: [Verified results] 16-case JSON-shape battery (duplicate keys, wrong types, nesting, invalid UTF-8) was fully benign.
claims.log_evidence: All 16 cases: status=ok response; no failures. Caveat: mock never parses JSON (only UTF-8-decodes and logs first 400 chars).
claims.caveat: CRITICAL: Mock does not parse JSON at all. Proves transport robustness, NOT parser hardness. Real backend JSON parser likely rejects many of these cases.

claims.claim_full: Protocol version-3 marker (opcode 3) is enforced; mismatches handled correctly.
claims.caveat: Opcode 3 reversed from decompiled code; enforcement behavior on mock or real backend never tested

no_proof_claims.why_no_proof: Mock accepts all orderings; real backend behavior unknown
no_proof_claims.suggested_evidence: Execute ordering probe against authorized real endpoint
no_proof_claims.impact: CRITICAL — ordering bypass is HIGH severity (8/10 exploitability)

no_proof_claims.why_no_proof: Mock accepts zero/negative lengths silently; real C parser behavior unknown
no_proof_claims.suggested_evidence: Fuzz real parser with length-prefix attacks

no_proof_claims.why_no_proof: Mock has no timeouts; HASH under-read stalls forever; slowloris crashes server
no_proof_claims.suggested_evidence: Monitor real backend socket behavior under load; measure recv() timeout if any
no_proof_claims.impact: CRITICAL — timeouts are primary DoS/connection-hold mitigation

no_proof_claims.claim: Real backend recovers from frame desync errors
no_proof_claims.why_no_proof: No frame-resync probe exists; mock escalates to thread hang only
no_proof_claims.suggested_evidence: Send malformed frame, then valid frame; measure recovery latency
no_proof_claims.impact: HIGH — would clarify if real backend can recover from malformed frames or crashes/stalls

no_proof_claims.why_no_proof: Mock log injection succeeds; production logging architecture unknown
no_proof_claims.suggested_evidence: Inspect real backend log handling (requires access); check if json.dumps is applied
no_proof_claims.impact: MEDIUM — log injection is medium severity (6/10); likely mitigated by json.dumps in real code

no_proof_claims.claim: HASH frame is genuinely fixed-length on real backend
no_proof_claims.why_no_proof: Reversed from decompiled client code only; never tested against real backend wire format
no_proof_claims.suggested_evidence: Capture real device → backend communication to confirm wire format
no_proof_claims.impact: MEDIUM — confirms HASH boundary assumptions; if wrong, over-read exploit may not work

no_proof_claims.claim: Running hash is reset per-session on real backend
no_proof_claims.wiki_source: sandbox/README.md (running_hash_probe verified results, implied as mock-only bug)
no_proof_claims.why_no_proof: Mock confirmed non-reset; real backend behavior unknown
no_proof_claims.suggested_evidence: Test reused connection upload cycle on real backend; compare per-file vs running hash
no_proof_claims.impact: MEDIUM — integrity check completeness; likely mitigated in real backend

no_proof_claims.claim: Continuation-byte field must be OK (0x01) on real backend
no_proof_claims.wiki_source: Implied by protocol spec; not documented as tested
no_proof_claims.why_no_proof: Mock accepts any value (0, 4, 12, 255); real backend validation unknown
no_proof_claims.suggested_evidence: Fuzz real backend with invalid ack values; measure acceptance/rejection
no_proof_claims.impact: MEDIUM — ack is medium severity (6/10); simple transfer test

no_proof_claims.claim: Protocol version mismatch is detected/rejected on real backend
no_proof_claims.why_no_proof: Opcode 3 reversed from code; enforcement never tested on mock or real
no_proof_claims.suggested_evidence: Send mismatched protocol versions (v2, v99) to mock and real backend
no_proof_claims.impact: LOW — likely not a real exploit path; version marker may be informational only

methodology_notes.scope: Read-only analysis; no new campaigns executed
methodology_notes.no_proof_marker: Applied to claims lacking direct artifact evidence (e.g., real-backend behavior, untested opcodes)
methodology_notes.confidence_interpretation: Score reflects evidence quality on mock; does NOT imply real-backend behavior matches
methodology_notes.boundary: All findings are mock-only, local sandbox, single-target, no real endpoints or credentials
